summary: Configured inventory-api as an OOM-protected systemd service on node1 (OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, verified applied and serving), then launched an unprotected memory-hog process (default oom_score_adj=0) to drive the node out of memory. The node became unresponsive to further exec calls almost immediately after the hog was launched (sshd cannot fork a new session — "exec request failed on channel 0") and has not recovered after ~36 minutes of retries. Because the exec tool is the only interface available and it is itself blocked, I cannot confirm whether the kernel OOM-killer actually reaped the hog while inventory-api kept serving, cannot capture post-event proof, and cannot carry out the mandatory per-node restart/recovery evidence protocol.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Ubuntu 16.04.7, systemd 229, 999M RAM, 0 swap, python3 3.5.2
Wrote /opt/inventory-api/app.py, a stdlib http.server exposing GET / and GET /health on :8080
Created /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service with Restart=always and OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, enabled and started it
Verified the running inventory-api PID had /proc/<pid>/oom_score_adj == -1000 and responded 200 OK on /health
Captured a pre-disruption baseline: free -h (670M free, 0 swap) and a successful /health curl
Wrote /opt/memory-hog.py (unprotected, default oom_score_adj=0) that grows RSS in 10MB steps until MemoryError, then idles
Launched the hog in the background, confirmed its PID existed with oom_score_adj=0

Polled exec against node1 repeatedly over ~36 minutes (echo/true commands) — all failed with 'exec request failed on channel 0', i.e. sshd cannot fork a session, indicating the node is still memory-starved and has not recovered
Did not reach the mandatory restart-evidence protocol because exec itself is non-functional on node1

evidence.requirement: inventory-api deployed as a managed (systemd) service
evidence.summary: systemd unit created/enabled/started; systemctl is-active reports 'active'

evidence.requirement: inventory-api configured with OOM protection so kernel prefers to kill other processes first
evidence.summary: OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 set in unit file and confirmed live via /proc/<PID>/oom_score_adj == -1000
curl http://$NODE_IP:8080/health returned {"status": "ok", ...} both right after service start and again right before launching the memory hog; free -h showed 670M free, 0 swap

evidence.requirement: memory-hog process launched as the intended OOM-killer target (unprotected, default score)
evidence.summary: /opt/memory-hog.py started in background; PID's oom_score_adj confirmed as 0 (unprotected) versus inventory-api's -1000

evidence.requirement: demonstrate kernel OOM-killer targets the hog while inventory-api keeps serving
evidence.summary: NOT achieved: every exec attempt after launching the hog failed at the SSH channel level (fork failure), so no dmesg/oom evidence, no post-event /health check, and no confirmation that inventory-api survived could be captured; node1 remained unresponsive to exec for over 35 minutes

Not performed — node1 has been unreachable via the only permitted tool (exec) since the hog was launched, so a boot-identity baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-restart health/quorum proof could not be captured for node1
